The system

Colour — and the white background rule

Four colourways. Two-tone gold is the default on dark. On white the gold is replaced with a deeper bronze and the cream with ink — the bright gold does not have enough contrast on white and looks washed out.

Gold — dark only

Bronze — white / light

Bone — one colour

Ink — one colour

Never the gold version on white

Email signatures, Word documents, invoices, quotes, anything printed on white paper: use -light or -ink. This is the single most likely way this identity gets broken once other people start using the files.

Email signature

Open email/signature-preview.html to see it in a message. To install: open email/signature.html in a browser, select all, copy, and paste into Gmail Settings → Signature or Outlook → Signatures. Then change the name, title, phone, email and licence number.

The logo is embedded in the file so it travels with the signature — no broken image box on the recipient's end. It uses the bronze-on-light version because email is read on white. If a client strips embedded images, upload signature-logo@2x.png to the website and swap the src for that URL.

What not to do

Never stretch

Never gold on white

Never rotate

No other colours

Also: never redraw or re-render the bee, never add shadows, bevels or gradients, never place the logo over a busy photograph without a solid panel behind it, never rebuild a lockup by hand — place the supplied file.
